bands.1:
There is no Keeper on Inkwell Bay. There is only Ghost Seven, and he is very tired.

Maxx's Content Factory is full of ghostwriters. They write all his words for him. They wear white sheets so nobody sees them. One of them, Ghost Seven, is on your side.

"The guards count sheets, not faces," he whispers.

So Indi makes ghost sheets for the crew. Mo's sheet says MO in big letters.

"Forty-nine, fifty, Mo," counts the Goldie at the door. He shrugs. "Fifty-one."

Inside, it is sad. Danglebys hang in jars over every desk. Asiflies are stuck in lampshades. The ghostwriters type, "Another Creature saved! #hero."

Zed types IWROTETHISMYSELF on the top door. It opens.

At the top is a gold box. Inside is a script. The cover says, "THE SORRY SCRIPT. In case I get caught. (I won't.)"

"Version 1: Cry. Use a real tear, not an onion."

"Version 9: Blame the intern."

"Version 14: Blame the Creatures. They wanted to be famous!"

"This is the worst thing I've ever read," says Mo. "And I've read my own recipes."

You put the script in your bag.

Downstairs, Wren opens every jar. The glowing Creatures fly away. The factory goes dark.

"Who turned off the lights?" yells a Goldie.

Gus lights a smelly yellow candle. "Earwax Candles! Three months of my ears. That's not gross. That's science."

You all walk out with the ghostwriters.

Outside, the Beamquid shines its light on a hidden hatch. Inside are a Tawnip and two Natterflits.

The sky fills with glowing Creatures. The ghostwriters throw off their sheets and cheer.

On the boat, you find the last page. One line is scribbled out. The Beamquid shines through the paper. Now you can read it.

"Version 27: Say sorry for what is on Deck 5 of the Vantadome. ONLY IF THEY FIND IT."

"What's on Deck 5?" asks Mo.

Nobody answers. Wren looks away.
bands.2:
There is no Keeper on Inkwell Bay, and no badge to win. There is only Ghostwriter Seven, and he is very tired.

Maxx's Content Factory is full of ghostwriters, who write every word Maxx says and wear white sheets so nobody sees them. One of them, Ghostwriter Seven, meets you behind the factory at shift change.

You flip it open.

"Version 1: Single tear. NOT onion this time. 'Vantafam, I made mistakes. Mostly other people's mistakes.'"

"Version 9: Blame the intern."

"Version 14: Blame the Creatures. 'They wanted to be famous, fam!'"

"This is the worst thing I've ever read," says Mo. "And I've read my own recipe book."

You tuck the Sorry Script into your bag.

Downstairs, Wren unscrews every jar. The Danglebys and Asiflies zip out of the windows, and the factory goes completely dark.

"Who turned off the lights?" yells a Goldie.

Gus lights a fat yellow candle that smells like old cheese. "Earwax Candles," he whispers. "Three months of my own ears. That's not gross. That's science."

By candlelight, fifty ghosts and a crew of fake ghosts walk calmly out of the door.

Outside, the Beamquid sweeps its beam across the factory and finds a hidden hatch. Inside are a Tawnip and two Natterflits.

The sky fills with glowing Creatures. The ghostwriters pull off their sheets and cheer.

Back on the boat, you read the last page of the Sorry Script. One line has been scribbled out. But when the Beamquid shines through the paper, the words show up.

"Version 27: Say sorry for what's on Deck 5 of the Vantadome. ONLY IF THEY FIND IT."

"What's on Deck 5?" asks Mo.

Nobody answers. Wren has gone very quiet.
bands.3:
There is no Keeper on Inkwell Bay, and no badge to win. There is only Ghostwriter Seven, who has not slept properly in a year.

Maxx's Content Factory is full of ghostwriters, who write every word Maxx says and wear white sheets so that nobody ever sees a real person going in. One of them, Ghostwriter Seven, meets you behind the factory at shift change, when fifty ghosts shuffle in.

"Two Goldies on the door," he whispers. "They count sheets, not faces."

That's all Indi needs to hear. Her disguises are bedsheets with eyeholes, and she has painted a number on every one. Gus's has a green stain where his last gadget leaked. Mo's says MO in huge letters, because Indi ran out of numbers.

"It says MO," says Tully.

"Ghosts can be called Mo," says Indi.

The Goldie at the door counts sheets as they pass. "Forty-eight, forty-nine, fifty, Mo." He frowns, then shrugs. "Fifty-one. Must be a new one."

Inside, the factory is worse than Seven described. Long rows of desks stretch into the gloom, and over every desk hangs a jar of glowing Danglebys. Asiflies are trapped in lampshades, blinking slowly, as if they're too tired to shine. Ghostwriters hunch over keyboards, typing, "Another Creature saved! I'm literally crying! #blessed."

The stairs to the top floor are blocked by a gold door with a keypad. Zed types IWROTETHISMYSELF, and it clicks open. "He's so predictable it's almost a bug," he says.

At the top of the stairs is a small round room, empty except for a gold box. Inside is a thick script tied with gold ribbon. On the cover, in Maxx's loopy handwriting: "THE SORRY SCRIPT. In case I get caught. (I won't.)"

You flip it open.

"Version 1: Look at camera. Single tear. NOT onion this time. 'Vantafam, I made some mistakes. Mostly other people's mistakes.'"

"Version 9: Blame the intern."

"Version 14: Blame the Creatures. 'They wanted to be famous, fam!'"

"Version 22: Cry until everyone forgets the question."

Mo reads over your shoulder. "This is the worst thing I've ever read," he says. "And I've read my own recipe book."

You tuck the Sorry Script into your bag. It's a bonus, not the main proof, but it's far too good to leave behind.

Downstairs, Wren is already at work, unscrewing jars and lifting lampshades. The Danglebys drift up to the ceiling. The Asiflies zip out of the windows. Without its Creatures, the factory goes completely dark.

"Lights!" yells a Goldie. "Who turned off the lights?"

Gus strikes a match and lights a fat yellow candle that smells like old cheese. "Earwax Candles," he whispers proudly. "Three months of my own ears. That's not gross. That's science."

By candlelight, fifty ghosts and a crew of fake ghosts walk calmly out of the front door. The Goldies are too busy bumping into desks to notice who is carrying jars.

Outside, the Beamquid is waiting under the jetty. It sweeps its beam across the factory and finds a hidden hatch in the floor. Inside are a Tawnip and two Natterflits. The Tawnip pretends to be a branch, but Wren carries it out anyway.

The sky over Inkwell Bay fills with glowing Creatures, swirling like a galaxy. The ghostwriters pull off their sheets and cheer.

Back on the boat, you read the last page of the Sorry Script. One line has been scribbled out so hard that the pen tore the paper. But when the Beamquid shines through the page, the words show up clearly.

"Version 27: Say sorry for what's on Deck 5 of the Vantadome. ONLY IF THEY FIND IT."

"What's on Deck 5?" asks Mo.

Nobody answers. Wren has gone very quiet.
bands.4:
There is no Keeper on Inkwell Bay, and no badge to win. There is only Ghostwriter Seven, who has not slept properly in a year, and who meets you behind the Content Factory at shift change, when fifty ghosts shuffle in and fifty more shuffle out.

The ghostwriters write every word Maxx says, and they wear white bedsheets so that nobody ever sees a real person walking in. "Two Goldies on the door," Seven whispers. "They count sheets, not faces."

That is all Indi needs to hear. Tonight's disguises are bedsheets with eyeholes, which makes this the first disguise she has ever designed that is meant to look ridiculous, and she has still gone further than necessary. Every sheet has a number painted on it. Gus's has a green stain where his last gadget leaked. Mo's says MO in huge letters, because Indi ran out of numbers.

"It says MO," says Tully.

"Ghosts can be called Mo," says Indi.

At the door, a Goldie counts sheets as they pass. "Forty-eight, forty-nine, fifty, Mo." He frowns. Then, because counting is hard enough already, he shrugs. "Fifty-one. Must be a new one."

Inside, the factory is worse than Seven described. Long rows of desks stretch away into the gloom, and above every desk hangs a jar of glowing Danglebys, so that the whole room is lit by Creatures who cannot leave. Asiflies blink slowly inside the lampshades, as if they are too tired to shine. Plumoths bump softly against the windows. Under them, the ghostwriters hunch over their keyboards, typing things like "Another Creature saved! I'm literally crying! #blessed."

"Literally," says Wren, and that is all she says.

The stairs to the top floor are blocked by a gold door with a keypad. Zed types IWROTETHISMYSELF, and the door clicks open. Seven, who did, in fact, write that password himself, looks at the floor.

At the top of the stairs is a small round room, empty except for a gold box on a gold stand. Inside, bound in gold ribbon, is a thick script, and on its cover, in Maxx's loopy handwriting: "THE SORRY SCRIPT. In case I get caught. (I won't.)"

You flip it open.

"Version 1: Look at camera. Single tear. NOT onion this time, a real one if possible."

"Version 9: Blame the intern."

"Version 14: Blame the Creatures. 'They wanted to be famous, fam!'"

"Version 22: Cry until everyone forgets the question."

"This is the worst thing I've ever read," says Mo, "and I've read my own recipe book."

You tuck the Sorry Script into your bag. It is not the proof you came for, but nobody could leave it behind.

Downstairs, Wren has already started. One by one, she unscrews the jars and lifts the lampshades, and one by one the lights go out of the Content Factory and up into the rafters: Danglebys drifting, Asiflies zipping through the open windows, the Plumoths close behind. Without its Creatures, the factory is suddenly, completely dark.

"Lights!" yells a Goldie. "Who turned off the lights?"

Gus strikes a match and lights a fat yellow candle that smells of old cheese. It is made from three months of his own earwax, and for once nobody asks him how.

By the glow of Gus's ears, fifty ghosts and a handful of fake ones walk calmly out of the front door. The Goldies, busy bumping into desks, do not notice that some of the ghosts are carrying jars.

Outside, the Beamquid waits under the jetty. It sweeps its light across the factory wall, finds a hatch hidden low in the floorboards and holds its beam there until Wren pulls it open. Inside are a Tawnip and two Natterflits. The Tawnip pretends to be a branch. Wren carries it out anyway.

Above Inkwell Bay, the freed Creatures swirl up into the twilight like a slow galaxy. The ghostwriters pull off their sheets and cheer, and Seven, for the first time anyone can remember, is crying with no onion in sight.

Back on the boat, you read the last page of the Sorry Script by Beamquid light. One line has been scribbled out so hard that the pen tore the paper, but when the Beamquid shines through from behind, the words come up clear.

"Version 27: Say sorry for what's on Deck 5 of the Vantadome. ONLY IF THEY FIND IT."

"What's on Deck 5?" asks Mo.

Nobody knows. Across the deck, Wren is holding the Tawnip, which has finally stopped pretending to be a branch. She has been holding it a little too tightly ever since you read the words out loud.
